chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, the compiler of this book, may God have mercy on him, says: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the most superior means by which servants draw near to their Lord, and what the most beloved of that is to God, Mighty and Majestic. So he said: 'I do not know of anything, after the recognition (of the Wilaya), that is more superior than this salat.'
Do you not see that the righteous servant Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: 'And He has enjoined upon me the salat and the zakat for as long as I live'? [Quran 19:31]

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat — the ritual prayer, the five daily prayers required of Muslims
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةِ: ma'rifa — recognition/knowledge, specifically the recognition of the Imamate and wilaya of the Ahl al-Bayt, the foundational Shia doctrine
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: 'azza wa jalla — Mighty and Majestic, a standard epithet for God in hadith literature
key_terms.يَتَقَرَّبُ: taqarrub — drawing near, seeking closeness to God through worship

ai.seo_question: What is the most meritorious act of worship after ma'rifa according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), establishes that salat (ritual prayer) is the highest act of worship after ma'rifa — the Shia theological concept of recognizing and accepting the divinely appointed Imamate. The Imam cites Quran 19:31, where Prophet Isa (AS) himself affirms that God commanded him to perform salat and pay zakat for his entire life, emphasizing that this obligation transcends prophets and communities. In the early Shia context, 'ma'rifa' specifically referred to the recognition of the Imam's authority (wilaya), making this hadith a key text establishing the hierarchy: doctrinal conviction first, then ritual practice.
